questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Invention] Why are some springs made from square metal?
A. To fit into square spaces
B. To reduce manufacturing costs
C. To enhance load-bearing capacity
Answer: C. The flat sides of the square wire provide more surface contact, resulting in a spring that can handle greater loads and resist deformation better.
questions.de: Was gewinnt eine Schraubenfeder aus Vierkantdraht gegenüber einer aus Runddraht im gleichen Bauraum?
questions.en: What does a coil spring wound from square wire gain over one of round wire in the same space?

timeline.labelEn: Robert Hooke first states his law of springs, 'as the extension, so the force', as a Latin anagram
timeline.labelDe: Robert Hooke formuliert sein Federgesetz „wie die Dehnung, so die Kraft“ erstmals als lateinisches Anagramm

source.title: Square and Rectangular Springs – Century Spring

questions.notes: Card's answer is right but its explanation is off: the gain comes from the larger cross-section (more steel in the same envelope, storing more energy per deflection — 'more force in less space'), not from surface contact; the flat sides mainly give a stable bearing area against buckling (Century Spring). Timeline: Hooke's law (Wikipedia, Hooke's law), as the spring has no date of its own.

questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] What are the gaps between nerve cells called?
A. Axons B. Dendrites C. Synapses
Answer: C. Synapses are the small gaps between nerve cells (neurons). They play a crucial role in transmitting signals from one neuron to another, facilitating neural communication throughout the nervous system.
questions.de: Wie heißen die Verbindungsstellen zwischen Nervenzellen, an denen Signale von einem Neuron zum nächsten übertragen werden?
questions.en: What are the junctions between nerve cells, where signals pass from one neuron to the next, called?

timeline.labelEn: Charles Sherrington introduces the word 'synapse' in Michael Foster's Textbook of Physiology
timeline.labelDe: Charles Sherrington führt das Wort „Synapse“ in Michael Fosters Lehrbuch der Physiologie ein

questions.notes: Imprecise card: a synapse is the whole junction between neurons; the gap itself is the synaptic cleft (Wikipedia). Asked as 'junctions' to keep the answer exact.
